newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-N.Z. A well placed vs England at tea.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-N.Z. A well placed vs England at tea.

text.p: WANGANUI, Jan 31 - New Zealand A were well placed at tea on the second day of their four-day cricket match against England on Friday.
At the interval, New Zealand A were 98 for two in their second innings, holding an overall lead of 172.
England had been bowled out just before lunch in their first innings for a paltry 107, 74 behind New Zealand A's first-innings 181.
New Zealand test hopefuls Geoff Allott and Heath Davis picked up four wickets apiece as England's batsmen failed to cope with some lively, penetrative seam bowling.

The only wickets to fall in the middle session were New Zealand A captain Darrin Murray, bowled for 12 by Andrew Caddick, and opener Craig Spearman, who was well caught at second slip by Nick Knight off medium pacer Ronnie Irani for 47.
At tea lefthander Phil Chandler was on 31 and Matt Horne had reached five.
